titleEn: Porcine sapovirus study first to evaluate a prescribed vaccine
titleZh: 首个商品化猪札幌病毒疫苗评估研究：新细胞系助力病毒分离与免疫应答分析
summaryZh: 猪札幌病毒（PoSaV）是影响各年龄段猪只的猪业新发病原，可导致断奶前后腹泻和体重下降。美国猪健康信息中心资助俄亥俄州立大学开展研究，首次在ST细胞系中成功分离PoSaV野毒株，并评估了商品化疫苗对母猪/后备母猪初乳和乳汁中病毒中和抗体滴度的影响。结果显示，疫苗接种显著提高了初乳和产后1周乳汁中的抗体水平，但未影响仔猪生长性能，且未检测到病毒排毒。该研究为PoSaV诊断工具和疫苗开发提供了新平台，但需进一步攻毒试验验证疫苗效力。
featuredReason: 该研究首次在ST细胞系中成功分离猪札幌病毒野毒株，并评估了商品化疫苗的免疫应答，为猪业新发腹泻病的诊断和防控提供了新工具，对猪场生物安全策略优化具有参考价值。

Porcine sapovirus study first to evaluate a prescribed vaccine

An emerging swine industry disease that can affect pigs of all ages, vaccine assessment against PoSaV is critical to prevent production losses.

Swine Health Information CenterJuly 15, 2026

schedule4 Min Read

National Pork Board

Porcine sapovirus is an emerging pathogen that causes diarrhea and weight loss in pigs during weaning and post-weaning. Because isolation of circulating field strains remains a challenge, the Swine Health Information Center funded a study led by Quihong Wang at The Ohio State University to characterize and isolate contemporary PoSaV strains and to evaluate antibody responses in the colostrum and milk of sows/gilts immunized with a PoSaV vaccine. Results indicate that a new cell line supports PoSaV propagation, a benefit to producers and their veterinarians seeking diagnostics, and confirm that vaccination boosts antibody titers in colostrum and milk, although future vaccination-challenge studies are warranted.

Read the industry summary of study #23-073 here.

As an emerging swine industry disease with the potential to affect pigs of all ages, the assessment of vaccine performance against PoSaV is critical to prevent production losses. Eight PoSaV genogroups have been identified, with GIII being the most prevalent worldwide. The isolation of field strains in cell lines remains a significant challenge to enable development of autogenous vaccine candidates for PoSaV disease control and prevention on farms. Therefore, the objectives of this project were to 1) isolate contemporary PoSaV strains in cell culture, 2) evaluate viral neutralizing (VN) antibody responses in the colostrum/milk of gilts/sows immunized with a commercial PoSaV vaccine, and 3) correlate the VN antibody titers with piglet performance such as body weight.

Related:Prepare for African swine fever and PRRS

Wang’s paper on objectives 2 and 3 was recently published in the journal Pathogens. Read the paper here.

To characterize and isolate contemporary US PoSaV strains, 42 clinically suspicious fecal and intestinal samples were collected from diarrheic pigs in late lactation across five farms for PoSaV PCR testing. Positive samples were then serially passaged in swine testicular cells, porcine kidney cells, and porcine intestinal epithelial cells. PoSaV replication was confirmed by testing both viral nucleic acids and antigens. Additionally, the genomes of representative positive samples were sequenced.

Overall, PoSaV detection rate was 60% (25/42). Representative GIII PoSaV strains shared 87.5%-87.7% nucleotide identity in the viral capsid protein with the prototype GIII PoSaV Cowden strain detected 40 years ago. The success rates for isolating field PoSaV samples were 8% (2/25) in ST cells, 16% (8/25) in LLC-PK1 cells, and 0% (0/10) in IPEC-J2 cells. Importantly, this represents the first successful isolation of PoSaV in ST cells, creating new opportunities for future viral pathogenesis and vaccine research.

Related:Researchers aim to identify New World screwworm vulnerabilities

For objectives 2 and 3, a commercial swine farm with approximately 650 sows and gilts operating on a 4-week batch farrowing system was utilized. A total of 30 animals were randomly assigned to two groups: vaccination and non-vaccination, with each group comprising 15 animals (two gilts and 13 sows). For the vaccination group, animals were immunized intramuscularly with a PoSaV vaccine at gestation day 73 – 75 (about 5 weeks pre-farrowing) and at GD 94 – 96 (about two weeks pre-farrowing). Body weights of individual piglets were obtained at birth and at 3 weeks of age. Colostrum and milk samples collected at parturition, one week, two weeks and three weeks post-farrowing were tested for VN antibody titers. Rectal swab samples from the sows/gilts and three piglets per sow/gilt at 2 weeks and 3 weeks of age were tested for PoSaV shedding.

All rectal swab samples from sows and piglets in both groups tested negative for PoSaV, indicating no PoSaV was circulating among these pigs during the study period. Both groups of piglets had similar weights at birth and at 3 weeks of age and piglet growth performance did not differ between treatment groups.

Related:Novus launches digital feed ingredient platform

Additional results indicated that sows and gilts within the same group had similar levels of VN antibody titers at each time point. Colostrum samples contained high VN antibody titers (> 10^4.5 VNT50/mL), with the vaccinated group having significantly higher antibody titers in colostrum (p < 0.01) compared to the non-vaccinated group. Further, the vaccinated group maintained significantly higher (p < 0.05) VN antibody titers in the milk at 1-week post-farrowing but had no significant differences at 2 and 3 weeks post-farrowing compared to the non-vaccinated group.

These results indicate that sows/gilts had been exposed to PoSaV natural infection prior to vaccination and that vaccination boosted the existing immunity. The high antibody levels in both groups of sows/gilts may have provided full protection for piglets against PoSaV infection at this farm, although the threshold level of VN antibodies needed for PoSaV protection has not been determined. These findings indicate that vaccination effectively boosted pre-existing immunity; however, additional vaccination-challenge studies are needed to determine vaccine efficacy in naïve pigs since no PoSaV shedding was detected.

Overall, this project advances understanding of contemporary PoSaV biology, establishes a novel virus isolation platform, and provides the first evaluation of a prescribed PoSaV vaccine produced under commercial conditions. Expanding the potential for PoSaV isolation in the ST cell line offers a promising avenue for the development of effective diagnostic tools and vaccines against PoSaV. Advancing tools for PoSaV aligns with SHIC’s mission to generate knowledge and mitigate the potential impact of emerging disease threats for the U.S. swine industry.

translationZh:
猪札幌病毒是一种新发病原，会导致断奶和断奶后仔猪腹泻及体重下降。由于循环野毒株的分离仍具挑战，猪健康信息中心资助了由俄亥俄州立大学Quihong Wang领导的一项研究，旨在表征和分离当代PoSaV毒株，并评估接种PoSaV疫苗的母猪/后备母猪初乳和乳汁中的抗体反应。结果表明，一种新的细胞系支持PoSaV增殖，这对寻求诊断的生产者和兽医有利，并确认疫苗接种可提高初乳和乳汁中的抗体滴度，尽管未来仍需开展疫苗接种-攻毒研究。

作为可能影响各年龄段猪只的新兴猪业疾病，评估PoSaV疫苗性能对于防止生产损失至关重要。目前已鉴定出8个PoSaV基因群，其中GIII在全球最为流行。在细胞系中分离野毒株仍是开发用于农场PoSaV疾病防控的自体疫苗候选株的重大挑战。因此，本项目的目标是：1）在细胞培养中分离当代PoSaV毒株；2）评估接种商品化PoSaV疫苗的后备母猪/母猪初乳/乳汁中的病毒中和（VN）抗体反应；3）将VN抗体滴度与仔猪生产性能（如体重）相关联。

Wang关于目标2和3的论文近期发表在《Pathogens》期刊上。

为了表征和分离美国当代PoSaV毒株，从5个农场哺乳后期腹泻猪中采集了42份临床可疑粪便和肠道样本，进行PoSaV PCR检测。阳性样本随后在猪睾丸细胞、猪肾细胞和猪肠上皮细胞中连续传代。通过检测病毒核酸和抗原确认PoSaV复制。此外，对代表性阳性样本的基因组进行了测序。

总体而言，PoSaV检出率为60%（25/42）。代表性GIII PoSaV毒株与40年前检出的原型GIII PoSaV Cowden毒株在病毒衣壳蛋白上具有87.5%-87.7%的核苷酸同源性。在ST细胞中分离野毒株的成功率为8%（2/25），在LLC-PK1细胞中为16%（8/25），在IPEC-J2细胞中为0%（0/10）。重要的是，这代表了首次在ST细胞中成功分离PoSaV，为未来的病毒致病性和疫苗研究创造了新机遇。

对于目标2和3，研究利用了一个拥有约650头母猪和后备母猪、采用4周批次分娩系统的商品化猪场。共30头动物被随机分为两组：疫苗接种组和非疫苗接种组，每组15头动物（2头后备母猪和13头母猪）。疫苗接种组在妊娠第73-75天（约产前5周）和妊娠第94-96天（约产前2周）肌肉注射PoSaV疫苗。在出生时和3周龄时获取个体仔猪体重。在分娩时、产后1周、2周和3周采集初乳和乳汁样本，检测VN抗体滴度。对母猪/后备母猪及其每头母猪/后备母猪的3头仔猪在2周龄和3周龄时采集直肠拭子样本，检测PoSaV排毒。

两组母猪和仔猪的所有直肠拭子样本均检测为PoSaV阴性，表明研究期间这些猪群中无PoSaV循环。两组仔猪在出生时和3周龄时体重相似，仔猪生长性能在处理组间无差异。

其他结果表明，同一组内的母猪和后备母猪在每个时间点的VN抗体滴度水平相似。初乳样本含有高VN抗体滴度（>10^4.5 VNT50/mL），疫苗接种组初乳中的抗体滴度显著高于非疫苗接种组（p < 0.01）。此外，疫苗接种组在产后1周时乳汁中的VN抗体滴度显著更高（p < 0.05），但在产后2周和3周时与非疫苗接种组相比无显著差异。

这些结果表明，母猪/后备母猪在疫苗接种前已暴露于PoSaV自然感染，疫苗接种增强了现有免疫力。两组母猪/后备母猪的高抗体水平可能为该农场的仔猪提供了针对PoSaV感染的完全保护，尽管尚未确定PoSaV保护所需的VN抗体阈值水平。这些发现表明，疫苗接种有效增强了预先存在的免疫力；然而，由于未检测到PoSaV排毒，需要额外的疫苗接种-攻毒研究来确定疫苗在未感染猪中的效力。

总体而言，该项目增进了对当代PoSaV生物学的理解，建立了一个新的病毒分离平台，并提供了首个在商业化条件下生产的指定PoSaV疫苗的评估。扩大在ST细胞系中分离PoSaV的潜力，为开发针对PoSaV的有效诊断工具和疫苗提供了有前景的途径。推进PoSaV相关工具与SHIC的使命一致，即生成知识并减轻新发病威胁对美国猪业的潜在影响。
